title: Latency for European callers
prompt: The on-call team wants a quick look at how fast the service answers callers in `eu-west`. What does this program print? Type each line on its own line.
program:
eu = api_requests.rdd.filter(lambda r: r["client_region"] == "eu-west")
latency = eu.map(lambda r: r["latency_ms"]).collect()
print(latency)
print(len(latency), sum(latency) // len(latency), max(latency))
hints: Find the requests whose `client_region` is `eu-west`, in table order.
`collect()` returns a plain Python list of the `latency_ms` values.
explanation: Three requests came from `eu-west`: REQ-000002 (38 ms), REQ-000005 (118 ms) and REQ-000012 (40 ms). `collect()` gives the Python list `[38, 118, 40]`; it adds up to 196, so the whole-number average is `196 // 3` = 65, and the slowest is 118.
